flaws.title: Same-tick one-for-zero swaps can revert because reset leaves an equal-range upward iterator pointing at a fake crossed tick
flaws.sequence:
1. The pool is at tick t where t is an initialized tick, and the active liquidity at t is small while tickLiquidityNet(t) is strongly negative because much larger liquidity ends at t than starts there.
2. A user executes the first taxable one-for-zero swap of the block, small enough that the pool tick does not change, so slot0BeforeSwap.tick() == slot0AfterSwap.tick() == t.
3. AngstromL2._oneForZeroDistributeTax calls TickIteratorLib.initUp(..., t, t), which calls reset.
4. reset returns early on equality after setting currentTick = t, so hasNext() is true and getNext() returns t even though no initialized tick was crossed.
5. CompensationPriceFinder.getOneForZero and then AngstromL2._oneForZeroCreditRewards both treat t as crossed and execute liquidity = liquidity.add(liquidityNet) for tick t.
6. Because liquidityNet(t) is negative and larger in magnitude than the actual active liquidity, the signed add underflows and afterSwap reverts, reverting the whole swap.
flaws.impact: Top-of-block one-for-zero swaps that stay in the same tick can be made unexecutable for users in affected pool states.

flaws.title: Inactive liquidity below the current boundary can steal swap-tax rewards on same-tick one-for-zero swaps
flaws.sequence:
1. The current pool tick is an initialized tick t, and the current sqrt price is already above TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick(t) but still low enough that a one-for-zero swap can finish with the same tick t.
2. Before the first taxable one-for-zero swap of the block, an attacker adds a very large inactive position [t - tickSpacing, t). Because upper bounds are exclusive, this position is not active at tick t and is not included in liquidityBeforeSwap.
3. The attacker (or any user) executes a top-of-block one-for-zero swap that stays within tick t, so AngstromL2._oneForZeroDistributeTax builds an upward iterator with startTick == endTick == t.
4. reset returns early, so the iterator wrongly reports one next tick: t. _oneForZeroCreditRewards then processes a bogus first segment from the boundary price at t to the pre-swap price and writes cumulativeGrowthX128 to rewardGrowthOutsideX128[t] as if tick t had been crossed.
5. The attacker’s inactive position uses t as its upper tick. Under standard inside-growth accounting, increasing rewardGrowthOutsideX128[t] increases that position’s claimable inside growth even though it was inactive for the whole swap.
6. Because the bogus growth is computed per unit of active liquidity and the attacker’s inactive liquidity is not in that denominator, the attacker can scale their inactive liquidity to claim rewards far larger than the tax from this swap, draining rewards that belong to active LPs.
flaws.impact: An attacker can siphon swap-tax rewards to an inactive position and potentially drain the pool’s accumulated LP reward balance.
